From Alfie to Wylie, you'll love these short, sweet and punchy British names for your baby boy.

Wondering if a British name is for you? If you prefer a shorter name, then you might want to check out this list of British boy names for one- and two-syllable options. Or perhaps you happen to love names that are sweet and punchy in a really adorable way — then, one of these baby boy names from England, Scotland and Wales might just be a perfect fit.

Want more British-inspired names for your baby-to-be? We’ve got brilliant options in the What to Expect app that are sure to suit your wee one.

  1. Adney. It's different but not too out there; in fact, it's pretty close to the more popular Andy. This English name means "noble's island."
  2. Alfie. Such a cute name for a little boy. It's a familiar form of the English name Alfred, meaning "wise counselor."
  3. Beck. If you're into one-syllable names, this is a winner. It means "brook" in the English tradition.
  4. Bowen. Owen is a super popular name these days — and here's a slightly different twist. It's a Welsh name that means "son of Owen."
  5. Chance. If you suspect your son will be a bold and brave adventurer who isn't afraid to live life on his own terms, then consider this stunner. It's a familiar form of the English name Chancellor, which means "record keeper."
  6. Dougal. This Scottish name means "dark stranger," and may give your son a hint of mystery.
  7. Eddie. Is Edgar or Edward a family name? Then you might be drawn to this sweet, less formal alternative, which means "prosperous guardian."
  8. Graham. Another masculine-sounding name that's short and sweet. It means "gray home" in the English tradition. You might also consider the Scottish spelling: Graeme.
  9. Hamilton. How about this classic name — which means "proud estate" in the English tradition — for your baby boy? Tony or Ham would make cute and unexpected nicknames.
  10. Jestin. Like the name Justin (which is a Latin name meaning "just")? So do a lot of people. Consider this Welsh version to make your son stand out from the crowd.
  11. Kai. A great name to pair with a long last name. It's Welsh and means "keeper of the keys."
  12. Ned. Here's another English familiar form of Edward. Plus, it's vintage-sounding, which might be perfect for your sweet baby boy.
  13. Smith. Yes, Smith is one of the most common last names of all time. But how often is it used as a first name? It means "blacksmith" in the English tradition.
  14. Tristan. If this name sounds like royalty to you, that's because there's a knight in the Arthurian legends named Tristan. It's Welsh and means "noise” or “tumult.”
  15. Wylie. This is a very cool-sounding name, and it suggests that its bearer may be quite clever. It means "willow meadow."

15 Oh-So-Charming British Baby Girl Names

by Kim Conte
Fact-Checked by Jennifer Kelly Geddes

Corbis
Bryce, Greer, and more cheerful baby girl names from England, Scotland, and Wales.

If you're looking for a joyful-sounding baby girl name to celebrate your daughter-to-be, there might be one (or several!) on this list of British baby names for girls that you'll love.

Hailing from England, Scotland, and Wales, these British names have more than sparkle and vivaciousness in common; like many British boy names, most of these names for girls can be shortened into cool nicknames that are equal parts fun and cheerful.

Want more charming monikers from across the pond? We've got endless baby name inspiration in the What to Expect app.

  1. Adeline. This English name could be pronounced two different ways — "Adelynn" or "Adeleen" — depending on your preference. It's a form of the German name Adelaide, which means "noble and serene."
  2. Bryce. This Welsh name could be used for a girl (think actress Bryce Dallas Howard) or a boy. It means "alert, ambitious."
  3. Dylan. Here's another gender-neutral name that's rising in popularity for girls and boys. It means "born of the sea" in the Welsh tradition.
  4. Ebrill. This beautiful Welsh name means "born in April." Due in April? Ebrill would be more than appropriate.
  5. Edie. Looking for something short and sweet? This familiar form of Edith — which means "rich gift" — may suit your baby girl perfectly.
  6. Georgina. If you want a name that lends itself to cute nicknames, this English pick might be the one for you. It's a familiar form of Georgia, which means "farmer" in the Greek tradition. You could call her Gigi or Georgie for short.
  7. Greer. This Scottish name is unique but still easy to pronounce. It would pair particularly well with a long last name. It means "vigilant."
  8. Henrietta. This is a strong, vintage-sounding name, which means "ruler of the household" in the English tradition. Etta would be a really sweet nickname.
  9. Joleen. How about a feminine name and a gender-neutral nickname? Joleen/Jo is the best of both worlds. It's a familiar form of Jolene, which means "God will increase" in the Hebrew tradition.
  10. Lynlee. This stunning English name actually sounds like two first names. It's a form of Lynn, which means "waterfall."
  11. Marjorie. We love this old-fashioned name that's coming back in fashion. It's a Scottish version of Mary (Hebrew for "bitter"). You could call her Marjie for short.
  12. Marlena. Yet another name that sounds like a combination of two… this one's an English version of Marlene, meaning "high tower" in the Greek tradition.
  13. Rosie. Considering Rose but want something just a bit more familiar and endearing? This English version could work.
  14. Starling. This English name — meaning, no real surprise here, "bird" — is ideal if you love the outdoors and want to cultivate an appreciation of nature in your little one. Plus, it's simply gorgeous, even shortened to Star.
  15. Teagan. This Welsh name means "beautiful, attractive" and like many of the other British names above, it could be used for a girl or a boy.

From the What to Expect editorial team and Heidi Murkoff, author of What to Expect When You're Expecting. 18 Chinese Baby Boy Names With Poetic Meaning

by Marina Wang
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton

Looking for a Chinese baby boy name that’s zippy — or zen? Take your pick from these poetic names, many of which evoke stunning nature scenes.

While many baby names in the West have long-established familial traditions, Chinese names typically get much more creative. Most Chinese names are a poetic amalgam of words that evoke beautiful imagery or aspirational character traits, referencing symbols of strength and masculinity or evoking powerful scenes inspired by nature. 

Whether you’re looking for a more sage, zen name or are a fan of the bright and bold, here are Chinese boy’s names for inspiration. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite Chinese baby girl names, too.)

1. Fenhua. A unisex name, Fenhua means “youthful and energetic.”

2. Haoyu. Parents with a passion for the cosmos might consider this strong baby boy name, which means “vast universe.”

3. Haitao. Have a strong love of the sea — and hoping your little one will, too? Try the name Haitao, which means “a strong and powerful ocean wave.”

4. Junfeng. There’s nothing more satisfying than finishing a steep hike to behold the breath-taking views. That’s the picture that this name paints — a majestic mountain scape seen from the ideal vantage point.

5. Lixin. A great name for a bright and sunny boy, Lixin (pronounced lee-shin) means “a glorious and beautiful sunrise.”

6. Lingyun. "Ling" means “lofty,” or “high up,” while "yun" means “cloud.” Choose this imaginative name for a boy who’s sure to have exceptional aspirations. 

7. Qianfan. A name that brings to mind nautical imagery, Qianfan (chee-an fan) means “a thousand sails.”

8. Shuchang. Shuchang is a great name if you’d like a gentleman with a happy demeanour. The name means “easy-going and blissful.”

9. Sile. Pronounced si-le, this name is for boys who are cheerful, optimistic, and always happy. What more could you want for your little one!

10. Sicong. Convinced your baby guy will be the next Bach or Einstein? Try out the name Sicong (pronounced si-ts-o-ng), which means “clever and original.”

11. Tianyu. You can’t go wrong with this very classic Chinese name, which means “heavenly jade.” 

12. Xiyang. If Lixin doesn’t quite do it for you, maybe try Xiyang (shee yan-g), meaning “the evening sun” or “sunset.”

13. Xuesong. Another name for nature lovers, "xue" (pronounced shoo-ye) means “snow,” while song means “pine tree.” Together the name evokes pine trees covered in a fresh blanket of snow: A picturesque name for a winter baby.

14. Yangfang. Perfect for a family with nautical proclivities, this name elicits the image of grand and majestic sails catching wind. A great name for your bold and adventurous little boy!

15. Yufei. A tranquil yet strong name, Yufei (pronounced yu-fay) means “feather in flight.”

16. Yulong. Meaning “jade dragon,” this classic Chinese name is a beautiful pick for your little guy.

17. Yuze. Pronounced yu-ze, this evocative name means “a refreshing monsoon after a humid day.”

18. Zhiyuan. Pronounced jir-yu-wan, this name sets the path for your ambitious boy. It means “visionary” or a “go-getting dreamer.”

Still hunting for the perfect baby name? Open the What to Expect app for the top 1,000 names (and plenty of unique ones, too) — plus get week-by-week updates on the tiny human you’re naming.


Written by Marina Wang

Marina Wang is a freelance journalist living in Calgary, Canada. On her off days, she will gladly eschew all responsibilities to sing songs and dance with her baby niece. Wang has a special interest in science and travel and has written for publications such as Science Magazine, Atlas Obscura, Mental Floss, Canadian Geographic and the CBC. She is second-generation Chinese and a native Mandarin speaker. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in zoology and a Master's in journalism from Carleton University.

by Marina Wang
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton

These graceful Chinese baby girl names evoke stunning imagery or have delightfully whimsical meanings.

Imagine flower petals blowing in the breeze or the glimmer of a firefly. Many Chinese baby girl names have enchantingly poetic meanings and evoke breathtaking imagery. 

Some of these gorgeous names are inspired by nature, while others bestow inspirational character traits like elegance, wisdom, or grace. Whatever your fancy, take your pick from these Chinese baby girl names for your little gal. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite Chinese baby boy names, too.)

1. Anhe. The word "an" is used to mean “calm and peaceful,” while "he" refers to a “water lily.” Think of a tranquil flower floating on a pond.

2. Baihe. Love lilies? Lily is a popular name in Chinese, too; in Mandarin, it’s Baihe.

3. Enya. This hip and modern Chinese baby girl name means “gracious and charming.” Bonus: it's easy to pronounce in both English and Mandarin.

4. Huanzhu. This ethereal name paints an image of a fantasy bamboo forest. "Huan" means “dreamy,” while "zhu" (pronounced joo) means “bamboo.”

5. Jingzhu. If you love Chinese landscapes, Jingzhu paints a pretty picture for your little girl: It means “peaceful bamboo.”

6. Manni. This easily pronounceable name means “a sweet and romantic girl.”

7. Meijuan. Pronounced may-joo-an, Meijuan is a poetic name. Mei refers to “plum blossoms,” while juan is “a lovely girl.” 

8. Meilian. Meilian is a botanical name that celebrates one of the most beloved flowers in China — the “beautiful lotus.” You could also call your little gal Mei (pronounced may) for short, a common character in Chinese names that means beautiful.

9. Meilin. A classically Chinese name meaning “beautiful jade,” this is an elegant choice for your precious little lady.

10. Mengtao. Another name with gorgeous imagery, Mengtao means “elegant peach blossoms in a sunny garden.”

11. Peiling. Hoping for an athletic and determined little girl? "Pei" (pronounced pay) means “strong,” while "ling" means “smart and bright.”

12. Shanhu.  If you love the ocean, you’ll get swept away by the baby girl name Shanhu — which is Mandarin for “coral.”

13. Shiyun. Poetic and abstract, "shi" (pronounced shir) means poem, while "yun" is “a cloud.” It’s a great name for a smart girl with lofty ambitions.

14. Yajin. If you’re looking for a strong and dignified name, Yajin is a sure bet: It means “wise and elegant.”

15. Yina. An adorable and minimalist name, Yina simply means “graceful girl.”

16. Yuechan. According to Chinese mythology, if you look closely at the moon, you can make out the shadow of a rabbit and a girl. Literally translated, Yuechan means “moon girl” — an homage to this Chinese legend. 

17. Yujia. Yujia evokes “a fine and gentle rain.” A spritely choice for a spring baby!

18. Yuzhen. For your precious little treasure, the baby girl name Yuzhen means just that: “precious jade treasure.”

19. Zhuli. A great choice if you love classic names, Zhuli is pronounced joo-lee and means “pretty pearl.”

Still looking for the perfect baby name? Open the What to Expect app for the top 1,000 names — plus get week-by-week updates on the tiny human you’re naming.


Written by Marina Wang

Oh Là Là! 16 French Baby Boy Names That Stylishly Cross Borders

by Ashley Parsons
Fact-Checked by Jennifer Kelly Geddes

From the trendiest picks to tried-and-tested classic French baby boy names, you’re sure to find your "joie" here!

When it comes to boy names, Latin, Greek and Biblical first names reign supreme in France. Many popular French baby boy names cross borders effortlessly, such as Quentin, Thomas, Hugo, or Pierre.

If you're looking for a French baby boy name, we've got you covered. Give this list of French baby boy names a spin. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite French baby girl names too.)

Still hunting for the perfect baby name? There are thousands to consider in the What to Expect app for your wee one on the way.

  1. Antoine. "Invaluable" is the meaning of Antoine in French — and what an appropriate name for the newest member of your family. Popular across France, it's common in the Loire Valley, famous for its fairytale chateaux.
  2. Aurélien. Taking off as a French first name in the 1980s, Aurélien, pronounced oar-el-ee-yen, is a great name for a baby who will grow up into a passionate young man. With the meaning "golden," or "shining," this first name can also be spelled Aurelian.
  3. Camille. A unisex first name, Camille is popular as a first name for both boys and girls. Saint Camille is honored the 14th of July each year, coinciding with Bastille Day.
  4. Corentin. From the stormy coasts of Brittany, Corentin is a name steeped in tradition. You'll pronounce it corh-ahn-tehn, and might spell it Corentyn, as homage to the Celtic influence in the region.
  5. Émile. Pronounced em-eel, this first name of Latin and Greek origins means "rival" or "obliging respectively." If you're familiar with Émile Zola's work, you'll appreciate this first name for your baby boy.
  6. Gaël. "Generous" is the significance of this baby boy's name. Gaël is a Celtic name with origins in Brittany. It is notably popular in the Brittany and Paris regions but present throughout the Hexagon.
  7. Jules. A popular first name in the Parisian region, the name stems from the Latin "jovilios," or "descendent of Jupiter." Boys named Jules are considered to have strong morals, a sense of justice and ambition.
  8. Laurent. This outdoorsy name means "carrier of bay leaf." Laurent is derived from the Latin word "laurus," or laurier (bay leaf) in French — a plant that grows wild in the hills of Provence.
  9. Loïc. Pronounced low-eek, Loïc appeared as a first name in the 1940s and saw a surge in popularity in the '80s.
  10. Malo. Another name from the coast of Brittany, Malo means "light pledge." Saint-Malo is also the name of a fortress and picturesque coastal town in the region. This first name, pronounced mal-low, has seen a wide rise in popularity since the early 2000s and is right on trend.
  11. Marcel. A name meaning "dedicated to Mars," this is an excellent first name for an Aries baby boy. This first name dates back to antiquity, but has come back into fashion — especially in Paris and Bordeaux.
  12. Maxime / Maxence. Both stemming from Latin, and meaning "the strongest," Maxime or Maxence are names that indicate strength. Several French writers, poets and artists carry these names.
  13. Olivier. Similar to the English Oliver, Olivier means "from the olive tree." It is common in central France, and pronounced like oh-liv-ee-yay. Reaching a peak of popularity in the '70s, Olivier remains a common choice.
  14. Romain / Roman. A classic French name from the Latin "Romanus," or "from Rome." It's equally popular in urban areas as in the provinces, making it a wonderfully versatile name. Both versions are pronounced roh-mahn.
  15. Thibault. Thibault, pronounced tea-beau, is a very popular first name in France. It means "courageous." You can get creative with the spelling: Thibaut, Thiebault, Thybault, Thibaud, Thibald, Thiebaut, Tibault, Thybaut. Choose the one that fits your child best!
  16. Valentin. From the Latin "valens," the first name Valentin signifies strength and vigor. It's pronounced val-ahn-tan and is a fine name for an active baby boy.

From Paris, With Love: 17 Sweet and Chic French Baby Girl Names

by Ashley Parsons
Fact-Checked by Jennifer Kelly Geddes

Stocksy
Looking for a name that's stylish, sophisticated, and feminine? Get inspired by these French names for girls.

You don’t need to know your "mére" from your "mer" to choose a French baby girl name for your little one. But unless you’re living in France or a die-hard Francophile, you might not be up-to-date on the trendiest French baby names. We’ve taken care of that for you.

From enduring classics like Juliette and Louise to emerging picks like Clémence and Manon, we hope you’ll find the perfect French baby girl name below. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite French baby boy names too.)

Looking for more unusual baby names? Head to the What to Expect app for all kinds of inspiration from around the globe.

  1. Adélaïde. Meaning “noble,” Adélaïde is a common first name in western France, near the border with Switzerland. Fluctuating in popularity, Adélaïde is a baby girl first name with Old World flair.
  2. Amandine. Pronounced ah-mahn-deen, this first name means “one we can love” — and love her you will! Common especially in the north and Lyonnais regions of France, this first name is distinctively French but remains easy to pronounce.
  3. Anaïs. A close cousin to Anne or Anna, Anaïs means “gracious one” in Hebrew. Rising to popularity at the end of the 1990s, new parents today still choose Anaïs, pronounced ah-nah-eece, as a first name for energetic and determined newborn girls.
  4. Aurélie. With a name that means “golden,” little girls named Aurélie are gifted with a sparkling first name, pronounced oar-el-lee. Similar versions of this first name include Aurély, Aurélia, and Aurélienne.
  5. Capucine. An almost exclusively French first name, Capucine has been popular for centuries and is back on the upward swing. Associated with the flower nasturtium in English, this feminine French name is pronounced ka-pous-seen.
  6. Cécile. Girls named Cécile are known for being strong leaders. This Latin-derived first name has yo-yo’d in popularity for decades, and is currently on the upturn.
  7. Céline. Originating from Latin, Céline means “heavenly.” With the rise of Céline Dion in the '80s and '90s it saw a peak in popularity, but its fame (and heart) go on; it’s often heard in kindergarten classes today.
  8. Chloé. A favorite in antiquity but only resurfacing in modern times in the 1990s, Chloé is an extremely popular French baby girl name. Meaning “young sprout,” little girls named Chloé are said to be curious and passionate.
  9. Clémence. “Mildness” and “gentleness” are the meanings of this elegant Latin first name, pronounced like clem-ance. As of 2021, it’s one of the most popular French baby girl names, especially in urban areas like Paris, Lyon, and Bordeaux.
  10. Constance. Another royal first name, many queens have borne the name Constance. Meaning “perseverance,” Constance is seeing a comeback among French baby girl names.
  11. Estelle. It’s no wonder the British Estelle has risen to such fame, with a first name that literally means “star.” This first name has been popular in France since the '70s and is still going strong.
  12. Juliette. Any French baby name list would be incomplete without Juliette. Though this romantic first name is not as popular as Claire or Léa, Juliette is a classic French baby name chosen in all areas of the country.
  13. Louise. Louise is the female version of Louis. Popular in the Paris region and the center of France, this is a royal name for a little girl who reigns in her household.
  14. Maeva. A name from the islands of French Polynesia, Maeva is a first name that went from unknown to wildly popular after its arrival on the mainland. This first name means “welcome.” Is it the right first name for your gorgeous little one?
  15. Manon. One of the most popular names in France, Manon (pronounced mah-nonn) is an exquisite first name for a little girl. A derivative of Myriam, this baby girl name is also chosen in many European countries beyond France, like the Netherlands and England.
  16. Mathilde. With a name meaning "conquering force,” your little girl is sure to stand up to life’s challenges. Mathilde is originally from the Germanic languages, but from the 2000s onwards has been frequently chosen as a French baby girl name.
  17. Marcelle. After fading out of use in the early 20th century, Marcelle is on the way back up in popularity. The name stems from Latin, “promised to Mars,” so it could be a nice choice for an Aries baby girl.

17 Epic Greek Baby Boy Names That Are Full of Character

by Helen Iatrou
Fact-Checked by Marygrace Taylor

Wondering what to name your precious little hero? Make sure he stands apart with one of these singularly Greek baby boy names, which are as meaningful as they are melodic.

While it's often common to name boys after their fathers in the U.S., in Greece, it has long been customary to honor grandfathers in this way. In recent years, however, Greek parents have increasingly tapped their ancient roots for names that carry a certain symbolism or fascinating backstory.

Here are a few of our favorite Greek baby boy names, many linked to mythical gods and heroes. (If you're not sure whether you're having a boy or girl, check out our favorite Greek baby girl names too.)

  1. Adrianos. This powerful-sounding name (pronounced a-dri-a-NOS) means "just" or "righteous." In the Latin tradition, it's written Hadrian, like the Roman. A superb name for a real idealistic truth-seeker.
  2. Aegeas. Most Greeks will tell you the Aegean Sea was named after Athens' mythical king Aegeus (eh-YE-as), father of Theseus. Some historians argue its origin lies in the Homeric word aix, which means goat. The ancient Greeks thought the waves of the Aegean resembled leaping goats.
  3. Andronikos. A compound name linking the words andros (meaning "of man") and nike (meaning "victory"), this baby boy name refers to a little boy destined to be serene and devoted to family. You might like to trim it to Nikos.
  4. Apollonas. Son of Zeus and Leto, Apollonas is the Greco-Roman god of the sun, light, music, and knowledge, and was known for his honesty and integrity. You may prefer to call him Apollo.
  5. Chrysanthos. Like a sunflower in bloom, this refined name literally translates as "golden flower" and can be shortened to Chris. Men with this name (CHRIS-an-thos) are thought to be exceedingly kind and sensitive.
  6. Faidon. He's the light of your life, so why not give him a name which underscores the fact? Deriving from the word "fos," it refers to the "brightest of all." The philosopher Faidon (FEI-don), a student of Socrates, was an educated, worldly, and sociable man who made friends wherever he went.
  7. Iraklis. If there was ever a name synonymous with big-heartedness and heroism, it's this. You'll know him as Hercules, Greco-Roman mythology's greatest and most beloved hero. Born to Zeus and mortal princess Alcmene, Iraklis courageously completed his 12 labors in order to achieve immortality.
  8. Nikiforos. This strapping name (pronounced ni-ki-FO-ros) means "he who brings victory." In ancient times, the term was employed as an invocation to all-powerful Zeus and love goddess Aphrodite. Cultured and a little on the serious side, he prefers spiritual pursuits but also knows how to have fun. His alias could easily be Nick.
  9. Nireas. If you and your partner spend more time on the water than on land, you might want to consider naming your son after the water deity Homer called "the old man of the sea." The son of Pontus and Gaea, Nireas was known for his wisdom and prophetic powers.
  10. Leonidas. While King Leonidas and his 300 loyal Spartan warriors may have lost the 5th century B.C. Battle of Thermopylae, his fearlessness will forever be the stuff of legend. His name conveys bravery, but he's also a romantic at heart. Leo is the pared-down version.
  11. Orestis. A mountain dweller, Orestis (pronounced OAR-es-tis) was the son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra. His name evokes simplicity and modesty. Beloved among family and friends, he is the conciliatory type who always tries to make amends with others.
  12. Orpheus. In antiquity, Orpheus was a mere mortal with musical skills comparative only to those of Apollo. He sang and played the lyre so beautifully that animals would pause to listen and trees would lean in closer to absorb his melodies.
  13. Perseas. This classic name (pronounced per-SE-as) denotes exceptional intelligence. Perseas is the much-lauded Hellenic hero who, dressed in a cape rendering him invisible, managed to slay Gorgon Medusa with the clever use of his shield to avoid being turned to stone. You could call him Percy for short.
  14. Paris. Here's a name for a heartbreaker. The son of King Priam of Troy and Queen Hecuba, Paris was drawn to physical beauty and the arts. His decision to name Aphrodite the most attractive of all goddesses in order to win the affections of mortal Helen triggered the Trojan War.
  15. Theofanis. This is an ancient Greek name that means "he whom God discovers or makes apparent." He might be considered a chosen one, but that doesn't mean he doesn't get a kick out of playing light pranks on his friends. Theofanis, Theo for short, is very much invested in enjoying the good things in life.
  16. Thiseas. An Athenian greatly admired for his success in doing away with all sorts of ancient monsters, Thiseas, or Theseus, was best known for defeating the half-bull, half-man Minotaur of King Minos on Crete.
  17. Zissis. Not only do you give life to your son but he will undoubtedly gift you with a lifetime of precious memories. Zissis is an ideal and easily pronounceable Greek name (ZI-sis) denoting "life" or "lifetime." Your little one is likely to be the only Zissis, or simply Zi, in the playground.

From Athena to Zinovia: 18 Enchanting Greek Baby Girl Names

by Helen Iatrou
Fact-Checked by Marygrace Taylor

Mulling over names for your darling little goddess? These Greek baby girl names convey strength, sweetness, and brilliance.

The Hellenes (Greeks!) have a truly limitless array of mesmerizing female baby names. Many are rooted in ancient myths and figures, like the Nine Muses. Others, fittingly, spring from the generous bounty of Mother Nature.

Hopefully you’ll find an option that steals your heart in this list of bright and bold Greek baby girl names. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite Greek baby boy names too.)

  1. Amaryllis. This irresistibly beautiful name literally rolls off the tongue (pronounced a-m-ri-LIS) and means "to sparkle or twinkle" like an eye. She sounds like the creative type who is always looking for ways to express herself. You might shorten it to Mary.
  2. Ariadne. The daughter of Crete’s King Minos, Ariadne (eh-rih-AD-nih) is best known for her role in the myth of Theseus and the Minotaur. With a name meaning “very pure,” Ariadne helped Theseus escape the labyrinth in which the fearsome half-bull, half-man resided. She became immortal when she married Dionysus, the god of wine and good times. Ari would be a cute gender-neutral nickname.
  3. Artemis. The daughter of Zeus and Leto, Artemis was the widely-revered, indomitable Greek goddess of hunting, wild nature, and fertility. She was also considered the protectress of women during childbirth. If you choose this name, send your daughter to ancient Ephesus to see the world’s most significant temple dedicated to her namesake. Her nickname could be Artie.
  4. Athena. A name that commands attention and respect, Athena was the bravest, most intelligent, and perhaps most enterprising of all the gods on Mount Olympus. Athens was named and the Parthenon built in honor of the goddess of wisdom, war, and the crafts.
  5. Avgi. She is the light of your life, so why not grace her with a name that translates literally as “dawn”? Pronounced av-YI, she may well turn out to be the early bird who catches the worm. 
  6. Avra. You already know she’s going to be a deep thinker and warm individual brimming with positive energy, so why not give your baby girl a name that means “aura”? It originates from the Greek word for a breeze that’s soft, fresh, and almost imperceptible.
  7. Dioni. Linked to Zeus, this name (di-O-ni) means “divine” and therefore, carries significant clout. According to some historians, Dioni was his first wife and the mother of Aphrodite, goddess of love. Dionne, as in living music legend Ms. Warwick, is the Americanized version. To you, she could simply be Di.
  8. Eleftheria. Linked to the Homeric era word “eleftherotis,” which means “liberator,” this uplifting name signifies a condition or power that is prized above all else: freedom. Ellie or Elle would make for a lovely nickname.
  9. Iakinthi. In Greek, Iakinthi refers to the hyacinth flower, whose fabulous blooms vary in color from ruby red to lilac. The name also means “precious gemstone.” You may recognize it as Jacinth, or the Spanish version Jacinta.
  10. Iliana. Popular with Greek parents, this sophisticated name means “daughter of the sun.” Some believe it derives from the ancient city of Troy, which the Greeks renamed Ilios. In the Hebrew tradition, it is linked to Elijah, which means “Jehovah is my God.” You might want to call her Illy.
  11. Ioli. She was the daughter of Eurytus, the king of Oechalia. Hercules’ love for Ioli (i-OL-i) led to his demise, but don’t let that deter you: This baby girl name is short but sweet and will set your little girl apart.
  12. Ismini. This playful name, pronounced is-MI-ni, means “knowledge.” In Greek mythology, she’s known as the youngest daughter of King Oedipus and Jocasta and sister to Antigone. Minnie would be an adorable alias.
  13. Melina. This angelic baby girl name is associated with the Greek word meli, which means “honey.” For the little girl who’s simultaneously sweet and tough!
  14. Niovi. This is a name for a self-assured woman. It’s likely derived from two Greek words, "nea" and "vios," meaning “young” and “life.” A perfect moniker for a little lady who will stay young forever — at least at heart.
  15. Phaedra. One of the most exquisite ancient Greek names, it means “radiant” and “happy.” What else could you wish for your young queen? Pronounced fei-druh, you might choose to call her Fay for short.
  16. Thalassini. If you feel most alive when you’re near the ocean, how about this rhythmical, spirited name? Thalassini means “she of the sea.” Take her to the beach while she’s still a toddler so that she finds her natural affinity for the water.
  17. Thalia. Yet another captivating ancient Greek name, it means “to flourish.” Thalia was one of the Nine Muses — the extensively-worshipped goddesses of the arts. The patron of comedy, Roman poets described Thalia as elegant and gentle.
  18. Zinovia. A composite of words, Zinovia hails from Zeus and means “she who lives and enjoys life.” This moniker is a close cousin of the name Zenobia — a queen who ruled over the affluent Arabian city of Palmyra in the third century and was famed for her ingenuity and heroism. Novi would be a neat nickname.

by Kim Conte

You don't have to be Irish to get inspiration from this list of charming baby boy names.

If you’re on the hunt for a magnetic name for your baby-to-be, scroll through this list of Irish baby names for boys. Maybe you have Irish ancestors. Maybe you just happen to really like Guinness and castles and Celtic culture and all other things Irish. Either way, you’re sure to find a charming name on this list.

1. Adan. Aidan, which means “fiery,” is one of the most popular names for boys, and who can blame all the parents of all the Aidans: It’s a darling name. But if you want something a bit different for your baby boy, consider this equally darling version.

2. Alpin. Cute, right? And it conjures up lovely outdoorsy images of forests and mountains. It means “attractive.” 

3. Brayan. Brian is a popular name (which means "strong, virtuous, and honorable"), but not as many Brayans (an alternative version).

4. Carlin. This name means "little champion" — appropriate, no? You could call him Carl or even Carley for short. 

5. Cass. Short, sweet, and powerful. This is a short form of Cassidy, which means "clever" and "curly-haired."

6. Cavan. It’s similar to Kevin — but, well, different, too. It means "handsome."

7. Dermot. Sure, it rhymes with Kermit (and it’s technically an alternate form of that name), but it’s more suited for a baby boy. It means "free from envy."

8. Donell. This name is similar to the more old-fashioned names Donald and Don while still sounding a little more modern. It’s a form of Donnell, which means "brave" and "dark."

9. Farrell. This sweet name means "heroic" and "courageous" — everything you’re likely hoping your son will eventually be.

10. Galen. This lively name means "little" and "lively." And for short? You could call him Gael.

11. Korrigan. This is a form of Corrigan, which means "spearman." How’s that for a historical flashback?

12. Lennon. Are you a Beatles fan? This would be a good way to pay tribute. It means "small cloak" or "cape." 

13. Rogan. Think you’ll be having a little ginger-haired baby boy? Then consider this name, which means "redhead." Awww.

14. Shane. One of the most Irish-sounding names on the list, this is one of the many variations of the name Sean, which is a form of John, which is actually Hebrew for “God is gracious.” Phew! Bottom line? It’s a terrific name.

15. Torrence. This is a bold name meaning "knolls." Toren would make a really good nickname.

16 Classic Yet Cool Italian Baby Boy Names for Your Bambino

by Elizabeth Heath
Fact-Checked by Jennifer Kelly Geddes

From trending names to tried-and-true monikers, these Italian boy names fit right in — whether you live in Italy or the U.S.

Our list of popular Italian baby boy names includes some that have been trending in Italy recently and others that are eternally popular. As with Italian baby girl names, we also like that many of these names have several variations.

Whether you name your baby boy after one of the great artists of the Renaissance or for your favorite soccer player, remember that in Italian, you pronounce every letter — though the pronunciations are often different than in English.

Want to explore more stylish baby names? You can find loads of amazing options for your bundle of joy in the What to Expect app.

  1. Alessandro. This eternally popular baby boy name in Italy softens the “x” in Alexander, a name which means “protector of men.” Sandro is a common nickname, as is Ale (ah-lay). Alessio, Italian for Alex, is a popular derivative.
  2. Angelo. The name means “messenger sent from God” — and naming your baby boy Angelo is certainly a nice way to give thanks for his arrival.
  3. Dante. The author of The Divine Comedy died more than 700 years ago, but his name is still on trend. Dante is short for durante, the Italian word for “enduring” and once a common first name. It’s pronounced dahn-tay.
  4. Domenico. Like Dominic or Dominick, Domenico has biblical origins, and means “of the lord” or “belonging to the lord.” And in Italy, there’s a cute, unusual nickname — Mimmo, pronounced mee-mo!
  5. Giorgio. If you're drawn to the English name George, you may also love its Italian version, pronounced jor-joe. We also like the fun nickname, Gio, pronounced joe.
  6. Giovanni. The Italian version of John has biblical origins, and John the Baptist (San Giovanni Battista) is a very important saint in Italy. Nicknames include Gianni (like Johnny) and Vanni. It’s pronounced joe-vanni.
  7. Leonardo. The name means “strong like a lion” and is of course most associated with a certain Renaissance genius who painted the Mona Lisa. Note that in Italian, the first part is pronounced lay-o.
  8. Lorenzo. Another name with ancient origins, Lorenzo was first associated with Laurentum, a region west of Rome. It’s the Italian version of Laurence or Lawrence — in Italy, Renzo is a popular nickname.
  9. Luca. This baby boy's name has a lot of history behind it. Its origins in Italian are linked to the Lucani, an ancient tribe from southern Italy, but in Latin, it means “bringer of light.” It’s a cute alternative to Luke or Lucas.
  10. Marco. This name’s origins refer to the Roman god of war, Mars. But Marco — Mark in Italian — is a common Italian name that also references San Marco (Saint Mark).
  11. Massimo. Max, Massimiliano or Massimo — they all come from the Latin maximus, for “greatest.” What a way to start your baby boy off on the right track!
  12. Matteo. For fans of Matthew, their English equivalent, the name Matteo has a fun Italian flair. Teo, pronounced tay-o, is a common nickname.
  13. Michelangelo. Pronounced mee-kell-angelo, naming your baby boy after the brilliant painter, sculptor and architect might give him some big shoes to fill, but you can always call him Mickey for short! Michele, the Italian version of Michael, is a derivative.
  14. Nicolo’. If you’re considering naming your baby boy Nicholas, consider one of the many Italian variations, each with a different pronunciation: Nicolo’ is nee-kol-O. Niccolo’ is nee-KOL-o. Nicola is nee-KOL-a. They’re all boys’ names (the feminine version is Nicoletta). For boys or girls, Niko (neek-o) is a fun nickname.
  15. Paolo. In the 1960s and 70s in Italy, it seemed like every other baby boy born was named Paolo, for Paul. San Paolo, St. Paul, is one of Italy’s most important saints, pronounced pow-low.
  16. Stefano. This popular Italian baby boy name is the equivalent of Stephen or Steven and is another name with likely Greek origins. It’s pronounced STE-fano, with the accent on the first syllable.

Written by Elizabeth Heath

Elizabeth Heath is a travel and lifestyle writer and editor based in central Italy. She is fluent in Italian and has lived in Italy for 12 years. She lives on top of a hill with her husband, bilingual school-aged daughter, four dogs and a turtle. Heath's work appears in The Washington Post, Travel + Leisure, TravelingMom.com, FamilyHandyman.com and a number of other outlets. She is the author of The Architecture Lover's Guide to Rome. Heath grew up in Florida, where she earned a BFA in fine art from Ringling College of Art and Design, a MA in humanities from the University of South Florida, and completed doctoral studies in archaeology and anthropology.

Bellissima! 14 Italian Baby Girl Names You’ll Cherish

by Elizabeth Heath
Fact-Checked by Jennifer Kelly Geddes

If you’re thinking of giving your baby girl a name that harkens to your family’s Italian roots, or you just want to choose a baby name that’s a little uncommon, consider these Italian baby names for girls.

Italian is a romance language, so it's no surprise that its feminine names often have flair. Even the Italian versions of common English names, like Alessandra (for Alexandra), sound romantic and dramatic.

Our list of Italian baby girl names includes some of the currently popular monikers in Italy, plus a few lesser used yet equally beautiful options. Oh, and here's a pronunciation clue: In Italian, there are no silent letters — so as with Italian baby boy names, you hear and pronounce every letter in the word.

Still searching for the perfect baby name? Check out the thousands of adorable choices in the What to Expect app.

  1. Alessandra. The Italian version of Alexandra, without the sharp "X" sound, has some pretty lofty origins — it means "she who protects mankind." That's a pretty cool name!
  2. Alessia. Like Alessandra, the name Alessia is associated with one who protects. It's the Italian equivalent of Alexis.
  3. Aurora. We like this one because it's pretty and unusual. Long before Aurora was the name of Sleeping Beauty, she was the Roman goddess of the sunrise. The name is associated with light and dawn.
  4. Celeste. Another Italian baby girl name with ancient origins, Celeste is associated with the Latin word for "celestial." It also means "sky blue" in Italian.
  5. Chiara. Pronounced kee-ar-ah, this lovely girl's name means "clear," or "clarity." In English, it might be Clare or Clarissa.
  6. Francesca. This eternally popular Italian name (whose male equivalent, Francesco, is equally popular) derives from medieval Latin and means "free." The ce is soft, pronounced che.
  7. Ginevra. Odds are low that they'll be another baby named Ginevra in your daughter's day-care class. It's not clear how the name Ginevra — pronounced gin-ev-rah — made it to Italy, since it's of Welsh origin. Can you guess its English equivalent? It's Jennifer!
  8. Giorgia. Pronounced just like Georgia in English, this popular Italian baby girl name also has its roots in ancient Greek, meaning "farmer." Whether your little Giorgia grows up to be a farmer we couldn't say — it's just a fun variation on the English spelling of Georgia!
  9. Giulia. The Italian equivalent of Julia (and pronounced the same), Giulia is a perennially popular girl's name in Italy. Its origins go way back to the founding of Rome: The Julia (Iulia in Latin) family, including Julius Caesar, were said to be direct descendants of the god Jupiter.
  10. Giada. Jade is already a lovely, unusual name, and its Italian equivalent, Giada, pronounced gee-ah-dah, is all the more unique.
  11. Noemi. The Italian version of Naomi (which is a Hebrew name) is pronounced no-em-ee and means "pleasantness" or "delight."
  12. Simona. "God has heard my voice" — that's what Simona means in Hebrew, from which the name originates. What a lovely way to give thanks for your new baby girl!
  13. Serena. This name means "peaceful" or "quiet." The ideal moniker for a future sensible and confident leader!
  14. Sofia. Spelled with an "f" instead of a "ph," Sofia is one of the most popular Italian baby girl names of the last 10 years. The name originates from the Greek word for "wisdom;" for Italians, it also refers to Saint Sophia, a Christian martyr.

Elizabeth Heath is a travel and lifestyle writer and editor based in central Italy. Top Baby Girl Names That Start With K

July 23, 2025
Latest update: See more
Choosing a baby girl name can be a difficult decision. Below are some ideas for baby girl names that start with K based on data from the Social Security Administration.
Back to Top
In This Article
  • Top 100 Baby Girl Names That Start With K
  • Baby Name Resources
  • Popular Baby Girl Names By Letter
  • Community Discussions

When it comes to girl names beginning with a K, the range of options is pretty vast. You may choose to go for a more unique name like Khaleesi, or choose an equally cute but probably more popular name like Kimberly. Another option could be to choose a K middle name for your special little girl. Some examples of women you may know with today's popular girls' names that start with K are:

  • Kimberly Kardashian (American socialite)
  • Kelly Clarkson (American singer-songwriter)
  • Kathleen Turner (American actress)
  • Kendall Jenner (American model)

From Kylie to Katalina, find hundreds of baby girl K name ideas — plus meanings, popularity trends, and parent favorites — in the What to Expect app.

Top Baby Girl Names That Start With M

July 23, 2025
Latest update: See more
Choosing a baby girl name can be a difficult decision. Below are some ideas for baby girl names that start with M based on data from the Social Security Administration.
Back to Top
In This Article
  • Top 100 Baby Girl Names That Start With M
  • Baby Name Resources
  • Popular Baby Girl Names By Letter
  • Community Discussions

These are the most popular girl names beginning with M and are guaranteed to make for a great choice for your baby. Although these popular M names are the favorites amongst parents, many can still be unique or have less common alternative spellings. No matter which name you prefer, these are all guaranteed to be cute names for your kid. Some examples of women you may know with today's popular girls' names that start with M are:

  • Margaret Thatcher (first woman prime minister of Britain)
  • Maeve Higgins (Irish comedians)
  • Marylin Monroe (American actress)
  • Matilda Wormwood (protagonist in the book Matilda)

  • Popular baby boy names by letter

Choosing a baby boy name is one of the first important decisions you'll make as a parent-to-be. Should you select a traditional name that will stand the test of time, possibly one that's remained in your family for generations? Or, should you opt for a more modern and unique baby boy name?

Fortunately, there are plenty of resources to help you choose the perfect name for your son. And believe it or not, the Social Security Administration (SSA) is a great place to start. Every year, the SSA rounds up the 1,000 most popular baby girl and boy names. The list below references SSA data from 2025.

Can't decide on the perfect name for your new bundle of joy? Run your ideas by other moms on the What to Expect app.

Here, browse the list of the top baby boy names for inspiration (or to see if your little one's name made the list!).

Key Takeaways
  • Choosing a baby name is a big deal, and whether you're going traditional or trendy, there's a massive list to explore thanks to the Social Security Administration's annual roundup.
  • The top boy names in 2025 include favorites like Liam, Noah, Oliver, and Theodore, but more unique names like Kasai, Akari, and Eziah are also rising.
  • With so many options to explore, this list is a great starting point whether you're naming your baby boy, looking for inspiration, or just curious about name trends.

What's in a baby girl name? It can be challenging to choose the perfect name for your daughter but luckily, there's plenty of inspiration out there to help guide this important decision, whether you go for a classic, sweet girl name or a cool and unique moniker.

A great place to start your baby name search is the Social Security Administration (SSA), which releases a list of the 1,000 most popular baby names for girls and boys every year. The list below references SSA data from 2025.

Can't decide on the perfect name for your new bundle of joy? Run your ideas by other moms on the What to Expect app.

Here, browse the top 1,000 baby girl names for inspiration (or to see if your little one's name made the list!).

  • The Social Security Administration releases a list of the top 1,000 baby girl names in the U.S. every year, and the 2025 data is packed with both timeless classics and fresh, trendy picks.
  • Names like Olivia, Charlotte, and Emma continue to hold strong at the top, while unique choices like Klarity, Rynlee, and Ailanny are rising in popularity.
  • With so many beautiful options to explore, this list is a great starting point whether you're naming your baby girl, looking for inspiration, or just curious about name trends.

15 Beautiful Biblical and Religious Baby Names

by Colleen de Bellefonds
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton

Getty
From Myra to Samson, check out some of our favorite classic Biblical baby names here.

Searching for a powerful-but-unique baby name? Whether or not you're religious, Biblical baby names like Estelle, Myra, Asher, and Samson have interesting meanings and aren't as common as many other names that tend to top the charts each year. Below, 15 of our favorite religious-themed baby names that are equal parts classic and captivating.

Religious baby girl names

  1. Ada. Coming from German, English, and Hebrew traditions, this punchy little girl name can be short for Adelaide and is an alternative to Ava; it’s one of first female names in the book of Genesis. You could nickname her “Addie.”
  2. Amina. “Trustworthy or faithful” in Arabic, Amina is the mother of the prophet Mohammed — making it a timeless name among Muslims across the world.
  3. Atara. Meaning “crown” in Hebrew, this little girl’s name is mentioned in the Books of Chronicles.
  4. Estelle. The French form of the Persian name Esther, this was the Jewish captive whom Ahasuerus made his queen in the Bible — as well as the name of a British pop singer-songwriter.
  5. Kala. Short for Kalila, or “beloved,” in Islam, this unusual but powerful name also stands for “time” in the Hindu faith.
  6. Myra. A Latin moniker meaning “fragrant ointment,” this little girl’s name appears in the Bible in Acts 27:5 and made an appearance as a minor character in the Divergent series.
  7. Olive. Love the uber-popular name Olivia, but looking for an original twist? This option is Biblical, appearing in Genesis; Sacha Baron Cohen, Drew Barrymore, and country singer Jake Owen all chose this name for their little girls.
  8. Rhoda. A fresh take on the name “rose,” this Biblical name — appearing in Acts 12:13 — also means “from Rhodes” in Greek.

Find baby name ideas you’ll love in the What to Expect app.

Religious baby boy names

  1. Asher. One of Jacob’s 12 sons in the Old Testament, in Hebrew this preppy name means “happy, blessed.” You can call him Ash for short, if you want to.
  2. Boaz. Used by the 17th century Pilgrims and still common in Israel, this bold boy’s name means “swift, strong.” It’s associated with the story of Ruth and Boaz, read during the Jewish holiday Shavuot.
  3. Bodhi. Meaning “enlightenment” in Sanskrit, the Bodhi is the tree where Buddha meditated his way to — you guessed it — enlightenment. This adorable baby boy name has been rising fast in popularity over the past years; it’s also what Megan Fox and Brian Austin Green called their son.
  4. Gidon. A form of the Hebrew “Gideon,” this tree cutter was the judge who defeated the Midianites in the Bible.
  5. Jokim. The Basque variant on the Spanish Joaquin (like the actor, Joaquin Phoenix) or the Hebrew Joachim, the name means “God will establish.”
  6. Omar. A classic Hebrew and Arabic baby boy name meaning “reverent” or “follower of the Prophet,” this traditional-yet-sophisticated choice might make you think of the legendary actor Omar Sharif.
  7. Samson. If you’re looking for a strong alternative to “Samuel,” this Hebrew name means “like the sun” and was the name of a judge and powerful warrior who helped the Israelites win their battle against the Philistines in the Bible. It’s also a song by the Grateful Dead based on the Biblical tale of Samson and Delilah.

15 Strong Russian Baby Boy Names With Sweet Nicknames

by Ashley Zlatopolsky
Fact-Checked by Lisa Lombardi

If you’re looking for a name that connects to Russia’s storied past but is still widely used today, consider one of these Russian baby boy names for your little one.

Looking for a classic, timeless name for your baby boy? Many popular Russian boys’ names exude strength.

As with Russian baby girl names, Russian baby boy names often come with an adorable nickname that can be just as appealing as the full version.

  1. Aleksander. Often spelled Aleksander in Russian, the derivative of the famous Greek name Alexander means “defender of men.” It was also the name of several Russian czars. A common Russian nickname is Sasha — perfect for your little one.
  2. Aleksei. If you’re a fan of Russian royal history, you might know that Aleksei was the name of the last heir apparent to the Romanov throne. It’s a name fit for a prince (or king) that means “defender” and stems from Greek origins, though it’s widely used in Russia and Bulgaria. In Russia, boys named Aleksei are also sometimes known by the nickname of Alyosha.
  3. Boris. It’s one of the first names that may come to mind when people think of Russian baby boy names — and for good reason. Meaning “battle” or “fight,” this powerful name of Slavic origin is consistently a top choice for parents looking to give their baby boy a traditional Russian name.
  4. Dmitri. With roots planted in Greek origin, this sophisticated baby boy name is a popular choice in Russia. It symbolizes “devotion to” or “follower of” Demeter, the Greek goddess of agriculture (also known as “mother earth”). Boys named Dmitri can also go by the unique nickname Dima.
  5. Grigoriy. You may be familiar with the American spelling of Gregory, but Grigoriy adds a Russian twist to this popular baby boy name. Grigoriy means “vigilant and watchful,” so it’s perfect for a future deep thinker. You can opt to shorten Grigoriy to the widely-used nickname Grisha.
  6. Igor. This traditional Slavic name given to boys throughout Russia and neighboring countries means “protected,” and in some instances, “warrior of peace.” It’s a cherished and beloved Russian boy name that only grows more appealing with time.
  7. Ilya. As the East Slavic form of the male Hebrew name Eliyahu, or Elijah, the simplified Ilya essentially means “the Lord is my God.” While the name may hold more religious meaning than some other names, it’s also used in neutral ways, making it a timeless Russian baby boy name.
  8. Konstantin. Depending on where you look, you’ll find different variations of this baby boy name throughout European cultures — including in Russia. Meaning “firm” or “constant,” this unwavering name is popular in Russia, Bulgaria and Serbia. A common nickname for Konstantin is Kostya, pronounced with a long “o” — as in, kohst-ya.
  9. Leonid. If you want a fearless name, there’s no better choice than Leonid. It symbolizes “lion strength.” While the name is of German origin, it’s a very popular Russian name too. Some nicknames for Leonid can include Leo, Lenya, or Lova (the last two of which are Russian).
  10. Maksim. What’s a perfect choice for a boy born to be a star? Maksim, which stems from the Latin name Maximus, which means “the greatest.” Though Latin in origin, it’s a powerful Russian name that comes with a modern nickname: Max.
  11. Mikhail. Like some of its counterparts, Mikhail is another regal name carried by Russian czars. The name is originally of Hebrew origin, translating to “who resembles God.” While Mikhail might be more formal, this name comes with an adorable Russian nickname: Misha (pronounced mee-sha), which can be gender-neutral.
  12. Oleg. It’s a short name that packs a lot of meaning. This East Slavic name means “holy,” “sacred,” or “blessed,” and it’s one of the most common boys’ names in Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. You may see different spellings of the name (including Oleh and Aleg), though pronunciation remains the same.
  13. Vladimir. This classic Old Slavic name is a tried-and-true Russian title. Meaning “of great power” or “ruler of peace,” this timeless name also comes with a fresh nickname: Vova.
  14. Yevgeniy. More commonly known as Eugene, the Russian variation of “Yevgeniy” quite literally means “well-born.” And if your baby boy is, well, born well, this Russian and Greek name is a perfect fit. If Yevgeniy feels a bit too long, you can shorten it to one of its popular nicknames: Genya or Yevgy.
  15. Yuri. As a Russian version of the name George, Yuri means “farmer.” It’s one of the simpler selections for Russian baby boy names, but that doesn’t make it any less beautiful. A unique and classic choice, many parents throughout Russia opt to name their male children Yuri.

When it comes to naming your little girl, Russian baby girl names offer some of the most beautiful and unique options.

With names that have stood the test of time, these classic choices — often ending in “a” — will guarantee your child will stand out from the crowd. Here are some popular Russian baby girl names to consider for your little one. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite Russian baby boy names too.)

  1. Alla. This beloved Russian and Ukrainian girl’s name (pronounced all-ah) has different meanings depending which origin you trace it to. In Russian culture, it represents “other,” while Hebrew and Arabic ties give it the meaning of “ascend” or “to go up.” Regardless of how you look at it, this simple yet stunning name is a classic Russian choice.
  2. Alina. Meaning “bright” and “beautiful,” Alina is a cheery baby girl name of Slavic origin that’s used throughout Russia and neighboring Slavic countries. It’s gorgeous on its own, or as the nickname Lina.
  3. Anastasia. You’re probably familiar with the name Anastasia from the famous Russian Romanov princess and Disney movie. This regal name of Greek origin means “resurrection” and packs a ton of power. But if Anastasia feels too long for you, you can also call your little one Anya or Anna.
  4. Anna. Though Anna is sometimes short for Anastasia, the name on its own has an entirely different meaning. This Latin form of the Greek and Hebrew name means “favor,” “grace,” or “beautiful.” Like Anastasia, girls named Anna can also go by Anya.
  5. Elizaveta. The Russian form of Elizabeth, Elizaveta is a traditional name with religious origins. Meaning “God is my oath,” Elizaveta (Liza, for short) beautifully rolls off the tongue and is a unique spin on its anglicized version.
  6. Lyubov. One of the most heartwarming names in Russian culture, Lyubov (pronounced loo-bov), means “love” or “she loves.” No wonder it’s a cherished Russian baby girl name. It’s just as popular now as it was a century ago, making it a timeless and modern choice.
  7. Maria. Famous throughout many cultures, Maria is also a classic choice in Russia. It was one of the names of the Romanov princesses. Maria means “star of the sea” or “wished-for child” — perfect for the new little gift in your life. Your little girl can also go by the adorable nickname Masha.
  8. Mila. You may link this name to the actress Mila Kunis, but did you know Mila means “gracious” or “dear”? A favorite Russian baby girl name, this simple yet tasteful Slavic pick is growing more and more popular in the U.S.
  9. Nina. It’s the name of a goddess — for your little goddess. Sharing a name with a Babylonian ocean goddess and Incan goddess of fire, this traditional Russian baby girl name can mean “grace,” “favor,” or “pure.” Some say it also represents the old Slavonic word ninati, which means “to dream.”
  10. Olga. This lovely Romanov princess name is actually of Old Norse and Scandinavian origin and means “blessed,” “holy,” or “successful.” It’s a charming pick that’s still popular throughout Russia, Ukraine, and beyond.
  11. Tatiana. The fourth of the Romanov princess names, Tatiana is a timeless and elegant choice for a Russian baby girl name. It’s said to represent “fairy princess,” which is appropriate given its royal roots. Girls named Tatiana can also go by the sweet nickname Tanya.
  12. Valentina. This stunning name is a feminine version of the Roman name Valentinus, which pulls from the Latin word “valens” and means “healthy” or “strong.” Though carrying an Italian pronunciation, Valentina is an extremely popular name in Russia — one that comes with the lovely nickname Valya.
  13. Vera. With Slavic origins, Vera simply means “faith.” It’s also associated with the Latin word “vera,” which means “true.” The name took root in the late 19th century and has climbed in popularity ever since, making it a favorite choice for Russian baby girl names.
  14. Yekaterina. If this name rings a bell, that’s because Yekaterina, pronounced eh-kat-er-eena, is the Russian version of Catherine (and also the name of one of Russia’s most revered rulers). Though the name is longer than others, it has a straightforward meaning: “pure.” It also comes with a slew of adorable nicknames, like Katya (arguably the most popular) and Katyusha.
  15. Yulia. This name never grows old, probably because Yulia means “youthful” or “love’s child.” This famous Russian baby girl name with Latin origins is similar in nature to Julia or Julianne.

17 Timeless Spanish Baby Boy Names

by Vanessa Petit
Fact-Checked by Marygrace Taylor

From Alejandro to Tomas, these bold baby boy names are both historic and popular throughout Spanish-speaking countries.

As we all know, a child's moniker is many things. You want a name that sounds aesthetically pleasing, sets your child apart, portrays a positive image, works well with your last name, and shapes an identity (no pressure!).

Spanish boy names are incredibly popular, and many parents love that these strong and sophisticated monikers have historic roots. Hopefully you'll find a name that rings just right in our list of Spanish baby boy names. (And if you're not sure whether you're having a boy or a girl, check out our favorite Spanish baby girl names too.)

  1. Alejandro. Of Spanish and Greek origin, Alejandro (pronouced aa-lai-hAAn-droh) means "man's defender" or "warrior." You might prefer to call your little soldier the shortened versions Ale or Alejo.
  2. Benjamín. From the Hebrew name Binyamin, Benjamín means "son of the right hand" and has also been used to name the youngest son of a large family. Take your pick of cute nicknames: Ben, Benni, or Benja.
  3. Cristian. If you're looking for a name that honors your cultural and religious roots, look no further: Cristian quite literally means "follower of Christ." You could, of course, always simply call him Cris.
  4. Diego. This Spanish baby boy name has Greek, Hebrew, and Latin influences and means "didactical and educated" — an ideal title for your future scholar.
  5. Guillermo. This Spanish equivalent of the English name William, pronounced gee-YEHR-moh, means "resolute protector."
  6. Joaquín. A biblical moniker of Spanish origin, this willful baby boy name means "God will judge." Joaquin (pronounced wa-KEEN) is also a saint considered to be the Virgin Mary's father.
  7. José. Of Hebrew origin, José is the Spanish and Portuguese version of Joseph, meaning "he shall add." This popular name is also used in many Spanish-speaking countries as a feminine second name (for example, María José).
  8. Juan. In many Spanish-speaking countries, the name Juan precedes a second name. For example, Juan Manuel, Juan Pablo, Juan José. It means "God is gracious" and has been a popular name for centuries — a sure bet for your little man.
  9. Manuel. The sweet nicknames for this moniker (pronounced mahn-WEHL) may be just as fitting for your little guy: Manny or Manu. From the Hebrew name Immanu'el, which means "God with us," this baby boy name was brought to Spain and Portugal in the 13th century as the Byzantine Empire expanded and has remained a popular name ever since.
  10. Marcos. Drop the "s" and you have the Italian variant Marco. Marcos originates from the ancient Roman name Marcus, derived from Marticos — referring to Mars, the god of war. This strong baby boy name was very common in ancient Rome, as in the orator Marco Cicero from the 1st century BC and the 11th century emperor Marco Antonio (husband of Cleopatra).
  11. Mateo. The Spanish version of the Hebrew name Matthew, meaning "gift of God," Mateo is one of the most important names in the sacred scriptures as the author of one of the four gospels. Your little guy can also go by the adorable nickname Teo, Mati, or Mat.
  12. Miguel. The Spanish and Portuguese form of the Hebrew name Michael — meaning "who is like God" — Miguel was one of the archangels who stood close to God and carried out his judgments. That's one powerful name for one wise little man.
  13. Nicolás. The classic Greek name Nicholas was derived from Nike, the goddess of victory. In Spanish, the "h" is dropped. Nicolas has been around since the 14th century, thanks to saints and clergy members with the name. You could, of course, just call him Nico or Nic.
  14. Pablo. The Spanish equivalent of Paul, derived from the Latin word "paulus," this name means "small, humble." Don't be fooled by the modest roots: Pablo was also a brilliant and influential Spanish painter (as in Picasso).
  15. Pedro. Pedro is the Spanish and Portuguese equivalent of Peter, derived from the Greek word "petros," meaning "rock." While the full name is always a solid choice, the nicknames Pepo and Pedri will make you melt.
  16. Santiago. You might think of the capital city of Chile, but this baby boy name, meaning "supplanter," is a classic moniker derived from Spanish santo (saint) combined with Yago (an old Spanish form of James). You could also call your little guy Santi or Tiago for short.
  17. Tomás. Tomas is a Spanish variant of the Aramaic name Thomas — and you might be surprised by its meaning: "twin"! The nicknames Tom or Tommi ring equally as nice.

She believes speaking two languages fluently is a superpower that allows her to communicate in two very different ways. 13 Spanish Baby Girl Names That Are Beautiful, Meaningful, and Timeless

by Vanessa Petit
Fact-Checked by Marygrace Taylor

These gorgeous and time-tested Spanish baby girl names roll off the tongue — many with your choice of sweet nicknames to boot.

Searching for a Spanish baby name for your baby-to-be? Whether you're looking for a name to honor your heritage or you simply like the way Spanish names sound, you've come to the right place.

As with Spanish baby boy names, Spanish baby girl names consistently top the popularity rankings in the U.S. Many are beautiful as well as adaptable and have powerful meanings. Check out our collection of favorite Spanish girl names for inspiration.

1. Alejandra. A warrior name, the Spanish version of this Greek baby girl name (pronounced aa-l-ai-hAAn-drah) means "defender of mankind." Ale is a sweet and common nickname in Spanish-speaking countries.

2. Ana. Derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, which means "God has favored me," Ana is a popular baby girl name used all over the world.

3. Camila. Camila is the Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish form of the name Camilla — a term originally used for a young person serving as an acolyte (follower) in ancient Roman religion. We love the nicknames Cami and Mila too.

4. Daniela. From "daniyel," meaning "God is my judge," the American version (Danielle) first appeared on the name charts in the U.S. in the 1970s and has held strong since. Try Dani for short.

5. Guadalupe. In the 16th century, Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe (Our Lady of Guadalupe) appeared in a vision to a man in Mexico. She's now a patron saint of the Americas — while Guadalupe remains a time-tested baby girl name. Lupe and Guada make sweet nicknames.

6. Isabella / Isabel. This Spanish and Italian variation of Elizabeth translates to "pledged" or "devoted to God." Isabella and Elizabeth have been interchanged in England since the 13th century. And you're sure to find a winner among the popular nicknames Isa, Bella, and Izzy.

7. Juliana. The feminine form of Julius (pronounced hoo-lee-AH-nuh) is said to be derived from the Latin word for "juvenile" or "youthful." You can call her Juli or Ana for short.

8. Lucía. Derived from the Latin word "lux," meaning "light," Lucia is a cheery name for the brightest new arrival in your life. This baby girl name is used all over Spanish speaking countries and was immortalized in a song by the Spanish singer and songwriter Joan Manuel Serrat.

9. María. Looking for a biblical moniker? It doesn't get more classic than the Spanish version for Mary, mother of Jesus. In many Spanish speaking countries, María precedes a second name (for example, María Gabriela or María Paula).

10. Mía. In Spanish and Italian, Mia means "my" or "mine" — but this multicultural name is also the Scandinavian and German form of Maria. It popped up on the top list of names in the 1960s in the U.S. and has since stayed a consistently beloved name.

11. Olivia. Records of this Latin name date back to 13th-century England. To this day, Olivia — meaning "olive tree" — remains widely used throughout the European continent. It also stands for "protector of peace," since olive tree branches in Christianity represent spiritual peace.

12. Paloma. This Spanish name means "dove." Pronounced puh-LOW-muh, it also suggests peace, as symbolized by the dove — perfect for your future diplomat.

13. Valentina. Derived from the Latin word "valens," meaning "healthy and strong," Valentina is the feminine version of Valentinus. Your cutie will have a plethora of punchy nicknames to choose from, too: Vale, Tina, and Nina.

Still searching for the perfect name? Download the What to Expect app for expert advice, daily tips, and a full library of baby names.


Written by Vanessa Petit

Vanessa Petit is a bilingual writer and translator. When she’s not writing, Petit is enjoying life with her two children and husband and planning their next family vacation adventure. Petit has over 20 years of experience creating content in English and Spanish for national and international newspapers, magazines and online platforms. She believes speaking two languages fluently is a superpower that allows her to communicate in two very different ways. She’s written extensively on education, parenting, women’s health, travel and beauty.

Fierce and Fearless: 9 Baby Names for Girls With Superhero Energy

by Siobhan Adcock
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton

Inspired to raise a leader — or even a superheroine? Choose one of these strong girl names.

No question, the world is a better place because of all the strong women who raise, lead, and inspire us. Expecting a baby girl and still haven't settled on a name just yet? Consider a moniker for the baby girl who will grow up to wield her own superpowers...like strength, wisdom, and compassion.

Here are superheroine-inspired baby name choices for the little girl who's about to change your world for the better.

1. Diana. Diana Prince is the fearless alter ego of one of the first major female superheroes, Wonder Woman. This classically beautiful Greek name, meaning "divine," is timeless and powerful. And of course, long before Diana was Wonder Woman, she was the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon.

2. Jean. Jean Grey is an empathetic and intelligent telepath from Marvel's X-Men series, and one of the leaders of the original X-Men. The name Jean, which has both French or English origins, means "graciousness."

3. Kamala. The 2014 re-launch of the old-school Ms. Marvel comic series introduced a Muslim-American teenager with superpowers named Kamala, a Sanskrit name that means "red" or "lotus." This beautiful name is also shared with Kamala Harris.

4. Kara. This Italian name, meaning "loved," is the alias of Supergirl, the ever-popular character created in 1959. Supergirl Kara Danvers has soared through dozens of reincarnations, including as the protagonist of the Supergirl TV series on the CW network.

5. Munroe. Another high-flying member of Marvel's X-Men squad, Ororo Munroe, aka Storm, is one of the most recognizable superheroines these days. The Scottish name Munroe is a subtle homage to the classic character, and a clever choice for a girl born to take the world by storm.

6. Mysa or Mhysa. In the Legion of Super-Heroes comic books of the 1960s, the White Witch was an otherworldly sorceress (real name: Mysa) who fought and flew alongside the likes of Lightning Lad and Saturn Girl. Mysa is a pretty name that evokes both a skilled superheroine from a vintage comic book era, as well as the powerful, dragon-riding Daenerys Targaryen of Game of Thrones, called "Mhysa" by her adoring subjects. 

7. Sage. Meaning "wise one," Sage is a strong, lovely name for a girl in its own right. The comic book star Sage is a lesser-known but powerful character from the X-Men universe with the mind capacity and analytical ability of a supercomputer.

8. Scarlet. The Avengers re-introduced The Scarlet Witch, a mysterious and magical heroine with telepathic, telekinetic, and seemingly tele-everything-else abilities. She's an old-school comic book star who has enjoyed a recent resurgence in popularity — just like the name Scarlet, either with or without the second -t, a strong name with a long history that came back from near obscurity in a big way.

9. Selina. Batman met his match in Selina Kyle, aka Catwoman, a fierce and formidable character who's been around since the 1940s and has been alternately a superhero and a supervillain. (It's complicated.) Selina, a baby name of French origin, has an equally layered meaning: It's derived from the Greek word selene, meaning "the moon" or "moon goddess," but perhaps also from the Latin word caelum, the word for "the skies."

Still looking for the perfect baby name? Open the What to Expect app for the top 1,000 names — plus get week-by-week updates on the tiny human you’re naming.

25 Unique Baby Boy Names That Make a Statement

by Anne Fritz
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton

Looking for an original name for your baby boy? From Ace to Ranger, you'll find a unique boy name you love on this list.

Expecting a little boy and searching for a baby name that isn’t like all the others? We’ve rounded up 25 unique baby boy names to help inspire you.

1. Ace. It’s hard to think of a name more associated with winning than Ace. It conjures up images of playing cards, tennis, and golf (among other games) and means “one” in Latin.

2. Alaric. Meaning “all-powerful ruler” and once common among kings, this German name is just starting to gain more ground.

3. Bartholomew. While this name may sound like a mouthful, it’s associated with lots of cute nicknames, including Bart, Tollie, Barley, and Art. Bartholomew was one of the 12 apostles in the Bible.

4. Cassius. As in Cassius Clay, boxer Muhammad Ali's birth name.

5. Castor. This is one of the Gemini twins’ names in Greek mythology, meaning “pious one” in Latin and “beaver” in French.

6. Cedar. This is one of the lesser-used “tree” names, and can be unisex.

7. Daxton. Similar in sound to the popular name Jackson, Daxton is French in origin and means “warrior who conquers great obstacles." Shorten it to “Dax” (as in Dax Shepard, Kristen Bell’s husband) for an adorable-yet-boyish nickname.

8. Finnian. This is the slightly more formal cousin of “Finn." Like that name, it's Irish in origin and means “fair.”

9. Gianni. The Italian equivalent of “Johnny” oozes European sophistication and means “God is gracious.”

10. Hiram. For parents who want a Biblical name that’s on the adventurous side, this is a bold choice. Country music fans take note: Hank Williams’ real name is Hiram Williams.

11. Kai. This Hawaiian name, meaning “sea,” is beautiful choice.

12. Lochlan. Another name rooted in both history and nature, Lochlan means “land of lakes” in Scottish and was used to describe Vikings long ago. An alternate spelling is "Lachlan," and it's rising in popularity (slowly) in the U.S.

13. Lynx. Like Fox and Wolf, Lynx is a strong, one-syllable animal name for boys, but its advantage is that it's not as common (yet, anyway).

14. Marmaduke. You may remember Marmaduke as being the goofy Great Dane in the Sunday paper comics, but this name is coming back into fashion.

15. Marquise. If you’re searching for a name that’s associated with royalty but is more unique than King, this one's for you.

16. Merritt. If you’re a fan of names ending in a double "t" but want something more off-the-grid than Beckett or Emmett, add Merritt to your list of possibilities for your baby boy. It's an Old English, unisex name.

17. Odin. This is one of the Norse god names that’s on trend, and offers a unique twist on the similar-sounding (and more popular) Owen.

18. Percival. Harry Potter fans are surely familiar with this name, which has strong English roots. But did you know that Percival was also the one perfectly pure knight of King Arthur’s Round Table?

19. Quill. This unusual baby boy name is of Gaelic and Celtic origin and is fitting for a child born to avid writers and literary types.

20. Ranger. If you like an active name like Ryder but are looking for a more unusual option, this update of French origin, meaning "forest guardian," might suit your son.

21. Rollo. Short, quirky names that end in “o” are popular for boys — this one is a jolly-sounding variation on the more common name Roland.

22. Rook. The tower piece in chess and synonym for “crow” or "raven" is part of the trend of familiar words being turned into baby names.

23. Sutter. Sutter is another up-and-coming “action” name for boys. While it’s associated with California’s Gold Rush, the word comes from Old English and means “shoemaker.”

24. Winslow. Surnames used as first names continue to grow in popularity, and this is a nice choice for your little boy. Winslow Homer, the American landscape painter, is one of the more famous men to have it as a first name.

25. Zephyr. Searching for a name that starts with “Z”? Zephyr has roots in nature and means “west wind” in Greek. It’s also the name of the mischievous monkey in the Babar children’s books.

Still looking for the right baby name? Open the What to Expect app for even more name ideas for your little one, plus tips from parents who have navigated this big decision too.

24 Unique Baby Girl Names That Are Anything but Ordinary

by Colleen de Bellefonds
Fact-Checked by Kathleen Felton
